note.question: How do network effects affect platforms’ business models in data markets?
note.overview: An incumbent platform first selects a data-based, subscription-based, or hybrid business model; an entrant observes and responds; platforms then choose prices and users coordinate on participation under network effects. The paper solves this sequential strategic interaction by backward induction with an explicit incumbent-focality equilibrium-selection rule.

components.label: Backward-induction platform business-model equilibrium with incumbent-focal user adoption
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Backward-induction platform business-model equilibrium with incumbent-focal user adoption. The incumbent moves first, the entrant observes and best responds, and the authors solve the platform-price and user-participation continuations before comparing incumbent payoffs. Because network effects can create multiple adoption outcomes, the model imposes an explicit focality rule favoring the incumbent whenever users can coordinate on it. Proposition 2 reports the resulting equilibrium business-model profile and market shares.
